prop:confinement-lp:
Proposition Confinement as linear program over the Hecke normal form basis. Recast the confinement operator selection as a linear program over the NF basis of H_3(q). This connects the categorical minimum-action principle to standard LP duality theory, providing a rigorous proof of uniqueness.

Primal program (operator selection)

The confinement operator \Phi = \sum_{i=1}^{6} x_i b_i \in H_3(q) for quark types (f_1, f_2, f_3) is the solution of:

  \min_x \quad \sum_{i=1}^{6} t_i \cdot x_i
  \qquad (\text{minimize Markov trace})

subject to:

  \sum_{i=1}^{6} x_i = n_{\mathrm{target}}
  \qquad (\text{net constraint})
  \sum_{j=1}^{6} G_{ij} x_j \geq 0
  \quad \forall\, i
  \qquad (\text{Frobenius positivity})
  x_i \geq -M \quad \forall\, i
  \qquad (\text{boundedness})

where t_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i) are the Markov traces of the basis elements, G_{ij} is the Frobenius Gram matrix, n_{\mathrm{target}} is the invariant net demand of the state, and M is a large constant.

The objective \sum t_i x_i = \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi) is the categorical action. The Frobenius positivity constraint Gx \geq 0 ensures that \Phi pairs non-negatively with all basis elements.

Dual program (deficit satisfaction)

By LP duality, the dual of the primal is:

  \max_y \quad n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot y_0

subject to:

  y_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{6} G_{ij} y_i \leq t_j
  \quad \forall\, j
  y_i \geq 0 \quad \forall\, i \geq 1

The dual variable y_0 is the shadow price of the net constraint. The dual variables y_i are the shadow prices of the Frobenius positivity constraints.

Strong duality holds because the feasible set is non-empty and bounded.

\mathcal{B}_3 as the LP solution

At specific topological evaluations, the LP has an optimal vertex at x^* = \mathrm{NF}(\mathcal{B}_3).

The Frobenius positivity constraints are tight at two indices (\sigma_0 and L_-), giving the two active deficit channels that correspond to the residual deficit.

Caveat: \mathcal{B}_3 is a local minimum

With the corrected Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(e^-) = z^3, the Gram matrix acquires a negative eigenvalue. The LP has a global minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. The Borromean solution \mathcal{B}_3 is a local minimum.

Quadratic extension

When the interaction involves a bilinear Frobenius pairing \langle \Phi, K \rangle_F = x^T G y, the optimization becomes a quadratic program:

  \min_{x} \quad x^T G y
  \qquad \text{s.t.} \quad
  \mathbf{1}^T x = n_1, \quad
  \mathbf{1}^T y = n_2, \quad
  Gx \geq 0

When y is fixed, x^T G y is linear in x, reducing to a standard LP. When both x and y vary, the objective is bilinear with degenerate G — at z = q^3/(q^2+1) the Markov–Gram form has a one-dimensional radical (the (1^3) block), so the quadratic program is posed on the quotient rather than on the full NF span (on the star pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j^*) the form is positive semidefinite with signature (5,0,1), whereas the bilinear pairing \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) is indefinite). Open scope. Whether the cone constraint G x \geq 0 above is imposed on the full six-dimensional NF span or on the radical quotient matches the open boundary of Term 4 of the six-term mass identity. The nuclear assembly step fixes y = \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{N}_{k+1}) and solves the resulting LP.
rem:confinement-nucleon-unit:
Remark Nucleon-as-unit justification from LP confinement proof. The confinement LP proof and the Gram degeneracy theorem jointly justify treating nucleons as atomic units in the transfer matrix chain. The proof is purely algebraic. The argument uses LP duality, Gram matrix eigenstructure, and braid group realizability. No physics assumptions enter.

Statement. The inter-nucleon transfer matrix uses nucleon strand types p, n with crossing coefficients pp: (1,0), nn: (1,-h_{\mathrm{A}}), pn: (1,-h_{\mathrm{A}}/2), without resolving the internal quark structure. This is exact because:

  1. LP confinement proves that the Borromean operator B_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 traps the quark NF coefficients in the Frobenius cone G\vec{x} \geq 0. No quark subset can unbind.
  2. Gram degeneracy (\det G = 0 at z = q^3/(q^2+1), the (1^3) block being the radical) shows that energy minimization has no interior strict minimum on the full six-dimensional NF span; the minimisation is well posed only on the quotient by the radical, where it attains its minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. Confinement at \mathrm{tr}_M \approx 1 is topological, forced by the braid group realizability constraint B_3.
  3. Consequence for the transfer matrix: Since quarks cannot unbind, the nucleon's internal braid structure acts as a rigid unit. The inter-nucleon crossing between nucleon i and nucleon j depends only on the nucleon types, not on the quark arrangement. The transfer matrix Skein polynomial P = \prod_i \hat{V}_i captures the full inter-nucleon physics at the nucleon level.
  4. Error bound: The nucleon-as-unit approach introduces no error for the transfer matrix. Quark-level effects manifest only through the nucleon NF coefficients, which are precomputed once.
prop:confinement-operator-selection: Proposition Confinement operator selection via topological Brunnian minimality. Among three-strand braid closures, the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is selected as the confinement operator by the topological principle of crossing-minimal Brunnian nontriviality. Its closure is the crossing-minimal nontrivial Brunnian three-link. The Frobenius Gram and Markov-trace data act as a consistency check on this topologically selected operator, rather than its selector.
prf:confinement-operator-selection:
Proof Topological selection of the Borromean confinement operator.

Topological selection versus operator-space cost

A topological principle selects the Borromean braid \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 as the confinement operator. The model encodes confinement, the requirement that no proper subset of the three quarks can be isolated, as the requirement that the braid closure be a nontrivial three-component Brunnian link. \mathcal{B}_3 is a crossing-minimal three-strand braid with this property (shown below).

This selection occurs on braid space, not on the Frobenius Gram matrix. A minimum-action functional on that matrix does not select \mathcal{B}_3. Because \mathrm{NF}(\mathcal{B}_3) is \approx 99.8\% the identity \mathbf{1}, any cost-minimising operator-space program selects the smallest-cost mesonic channel L_\pm. The Gram and Markov-trace data serve strictly as a consistency check.

Three unconfined quarks are unstable

In H_3(q), the unconfined proton quarks (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}) yield the product of typed crossing elements:

  \mathrm{NF}(\sigma_0 \cdot (\sigma_0 - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}) \cdot (\sigma_1 - \tfrac{1}{2}h_{\mathrm{A}}))
  =
  -0.105\,\mathbf{1} - 0.011\sigma_0 + 1.000\sigma_1 + 0.105 L_+.

The demand profile \{[\mathbf{1}] = -0.105, \sigma_0 = -0.011\} (with [\mathbf{1}] the coefficient of the identity word \mathbf{1}) signals instability. The unconfined state requires vacuum energy (\mathbf{1}) and crossing content (\sigma_0) from its environment.

For unconfined neutron quarks (\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{d}):

  \mathrm{NF}(\text{unconfined } \mathfrak{n})
  =
  -0.211\,\mathbf{1} + 1.011\sigma_1,

with demand \{[\mathbf{1}] = -0.211\}. This larger vacuum deficit reflects the extra down quark's -h_{\mathrm{A}} shift.

Candidate operator comparison

Evaluate nine candidate confinement operators by applying each to the typed crossings and measuring three quantities:

  1. Net constraint: |\mathrm{net}(\Phi \cdot \mathrm{crossings}) - \mathrm{net}_{\mathrm{target}}|
  2. Markov trace: \mathrm{tr}_M(\Phi \cdot \mathrm{crossings}) (categorical action)
  3. Demand channels: number of negative NF coefficients in the confined state

Naive ranking. Minimising demand channels and then \mathfrak{E}_\times selects L_+. L_+ represents a pairwise binding. An operator-space cost-minimisation falls into this channel, which the Brunnian requirement excludes.

Topological selection. The closure of \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is the Borromean rings: three components, all pairwise linking numbers zero, and every two-component sublink the unlink, so it is a nontrivial Brunnian link [kawauchi1996]. (The braid-level form of this statement is the Brunnian Borromean conjecture.) No three-strand braid with fewer than six crossings closes to a nontrivial three-component Brunnian link. The closure of such a braid is a three-component link of crossing number at most five. In the Rolfsen table every prime link with three components has at least six crossings [rolfsen], so the closure is split or composite. A Brunnian link has every proper sublink trivial. A split three-component link that is not the unlink has a nontrivial proper sublink: a knotted component, or a split-off linked pair. A composite three-component link of crossing number at most five is the connected sum of two Hopf links, and its two end components form a Hopf link. In neither case is the link nontrivially Brunnian. This selection uses no physical input; the comparison of \mathrm{net} values with physical data lies outside the proof (see the physical-interpretation remark following this proof).
rem:confinement-operator-selection-inter:
Remark Confined-demand beta decay and confinement universality.

Beta decay emerges from the confined deficit

The \mathcal{B}_3-confined proton NF has residual deficit:

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathfrak{p})
  =
  \underbrace{-0.100}_{[\mathbf{1}] < 0}\,\mathbf{1} + 0.036\sigma_0 + 0.998\sigma_1 + 0.099 L_+ + 0.009 L_- + \underbrace{-0.043}_{e^- < 0}e^-.
  • [\mathbf{1}] < 0, where [\mathbf{1}] is the coefficient of the identity word \mathbf{1}: vacuum energy deficit—the source of the nucleon's mass.
  • e^- < 0: electron-word deficit—the coefficient of the basis word \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (the electron, whose closure is the Hopf link) is negative, so the nucleon possesses a topological deficit corresponding to an electron. This is the categorical beta decay channel.

For the neutron, the deficit is larger: [\mathbf{1}] = -0.202, L_+ = -0.010, e^- = -0.044. The additional L_+ deficit and larger [\mathbf{1}] deficit provide the energy that drives \mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p} + e^- + \bar\nu.

The confined nucleon NF depends only on q_0 and the quark types. It is independent of the photon polarization (\varphi_0, \varphi_1, \varphi_{01}) that created the quarks.

This check is a comparison with physical data and is not part of the proof of the selection. Among the candidate operators, the topologically selected \mathcal{B}_3 has the smallest |\Delta\mathrm{net}|, and it confines. The cost-minimising channel L_+ gives \mathrm{net} \approx 1.22, which is far from the proton target. The identity leaves the quark demand profile unchanged.

conj:confinement-frobenius-reciprocity:
Conjecture Confinement Frobenius reciprocity: bound-state observables as G^{-1}-weighted dual pairings. Conditional on stationarity. Let T \in H_n(q) be a confined bound-state operator selected by the operator-selection LP with primal optimum T = \sum_i x_i^* b_i and dual optimum (y_0^*, y^*). Here, \{b_1, \ldots, b_d\} is the normal form basis, G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) is the Frobenius Gram matrix, and the LP-active set is:

  A^*(T) \;=\; \{\, i \in \{1, \ldots, d\} \;:\; y_i^* > 0 \,\}.

For every observable O \in H_n(q), the physical expectation value of O in the bound state T is the Gram-inverse dual pairing weighted by LP-active shadow prices:

  \boxed{\;
    \langle O \rangle_T
    \;\equiv\;
    O(T)
    \;=\;
    \sum_{i,\,j \,\in\, A^*(T)}
      u_i^*\,(G^{-1})_{ij}\,\langle O,\, b_j\rangle
  \;}

where u_i^* = y_i^* are the LP shadow prices on the active channels and (G^{-1})_{ij} is the Frobenius dual-basis matrix on the |A^*(T)|-dimensional active subspace. Equivalently:

  \langle O \rangle_T
  \;=\;
  \langle O,\, G^{-1}\,u^*\rangle_{A^*}
  \;=\;
  \langle O,\, T^\vee\rangle,

where T^\vee = \sum_{i,j \in A^*} u_i^* (G^{-1})_{ij}\,b_j is the Frobenius dual of T on the active subspace.

Sketch of Proof

The proof has two parts.

Part 1: Frobenius reciprocity on H_n(q). The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M is a non-degenerate Frobenius form on H_n(q). The Frobenius dual T^\vee of any element T is defined by \langle T^\vee,\, b_j\rangle = x_j^*. Solving this linear system gives T^\vee = \sum_{i,j} x_i^* (G^{-1})_{ij}\, b_j. Frobenius reciprocity asserts \langle O, T\rangle_{\text{phys}} = \langle O, T^\vee\rangle.

Part 2: LP-active reduction. The operator-selection LP yields the primal–dual pair (x^*, y^*) with strong duality \sum_i t_i x_i^* = n_{\mathrm{target}} y_0^*. Complementary slackness forces y_i^* x_i^{(\text{slack})} = 0 for every i. The boxed formula would follow from the substitution x_i^* = (G^{-1} u^*)_i on the active set A^*(T), which is not justified by the linear program (see the open step below).

The open step. The substitution x_i^* = (G^{-1} u^*)_i on A^*(T), with x_i^* = 0 off it, is not a consequence of the linear program. The optimality conditions of a linear program are feasibility and complementary slackness; x^* = G^{-1} u^* is the stationarity condition of a quadratic program. Granting that stationarity, together with the linearity \langle O \rangle_T = \sum_j x_j^* \langle O, b_j \rangle and the symmetry of G^{-1}, the boxed formula follows, as do i \in A^*(T) \Leftrightarrow u_i^* > 0 and A^*(T) \neq \emptyset for a nonzero optimum. Strong duality for the linear program itself is addressed separately in the LP-duality analysis.
rem:confinement-frobenius-reciprocity-in:
Remark Master formula: ingredients, corollaries, computational protocol.

Discussion

This conjecture, if it holds, provides the master formula for computing numerical predictions about a confined bound state of H_n(q). It governs binding energies, form factors, axial couplings, and magnetic moments.

Three distinct ingredients are required.

  1. The Frobenius Gram inverse G^{-1} (read on the quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, where the induced pairing is non-degenerate; on H_n itself \det G = 0 exactly, the (1^3) block being the radical). The naïve Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M(O \cdot \rho(\beta_T)) is not the physical expectation value of O. The Markov form is non-orthonormal on the NF basis, so dualisation requires the Gram inverse.
  2. The LP-active set A^*(T). Most of the d = n! NF basis elements have zero shadow price (y_i^* = 0). Including them in the dual pairing pollutes the observable with off-shell contributions. Only the active channels carry physical weight.
  3. The shadow prices u_i^* = y_i^*. By LP duality, the shadow price on channel i is the marginal cost of saturating the Frobenius positivity constraint. These prices are exactly the weights that make \langle O\rangle_T coincide with the physical expectation.

Corollaries

  • Corollary (g_A as an instance). The axial coupling g_A = \langle \sigma_A\rangle_{\mathfrak{p}} / \langle \sigma_V\rangle_{\mathfrak{p}} of the proton bound state is the ratio of two instances of the master formula at the LP-active set A^*(\mathcal{B}_3).
  • Corollary (raw conjugation traces are zero-information). The pattern \mathrm{tr}_M(\beta \cdot X \cdot \beta^{-1}) is cyclically equal to \mathrm{tr}_M(X) and independent of \beta. The conjugation pattern must be replaced with the master formula.

Evaluation Protocol

The rigorous evaluation of the master formula requires:

  1. G, G^{-1}: Evaluate the Frobenius Gram matrix and its inverse on the NF basis, restricted to the surviving two-row blocks (at z = q^3/(q^2+1), G is singular on all of H_n with \det G = 0, so the inverse exists only on H_n/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n).
  2. Active set and shadow prices: Solve the operator-selection linear program to obtain A^* and u_i^* = y_i^*.
  3. Observable coefficients \langle O, b_j\rangle: Compute \mathrm{tr}_M(O \cdot b_j) for each active j.
  4. Pair: Compute \langle O\rangle_T = \sum_{i,j \in A^*} u_i^* (G^{-1})_{ij} \langle O, b_j\rangle, with the active set A^* inside the non-degenerate quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}.
rem:confinement-sdp-spectral-gap:
Remark SDP feasibility as Hecke spectral-gap condition. Feasibility of the confinement SDP is equivalent to a Hecke spectral-gap condition: the feasible cone is non-empty if and only if

  \Delta_{\sigma}(q) \;:=\; \lvert q + q^{-1} \rvert \;>\; 0.

The Hecke generator \sigma on V \otimes V has non-degenerate eigenvalues (q, -q^{-1}) on S^{2} V \oplus \Lambda^{2} V. The dual certificate at optimum is the pair of Jones--Wenzl projectors onto these two isotypic components. The SDP's complementary-slackness matrix is their orthogonal decomposition.

Deconfinement. When q \to \pm i, \Delta_{\sigma}(q) \to 0 and the feasible cone collapses. The SDP retains its role as a numerical certificate at a given q. However, its existence is guaranteed by the categorical volume constraint and follows from the eigenvalue structure alone.
rem:confinement-sdp-multi-operator:
Remark Multi-operator binding from active dual support. Let P_1 and P_2 be confined particles whose composite satisfies the confinement SDP. Their binding subword is

  W_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\lambda \in \mathcal{S}^*} y_\lambda^* \cdot \pi_\lambda \cdot \Phi^*

where \mathcal{S}^* = \{\lambda : y_\lambda^* > 0\} is the active support at optimum. The cardinality |\mathcal{S}^*| \ge 1 is the binding multiplicity:

  • |\mathcal{S}^*| = 1 is the scalar LP regime (single-channel binding).
  • |\mathcal{S}^*| \ge 2 is the generic multi-operator regime. It includes all shell-closure and magic-number configurations.

The optimality identity

  \Phi^* \cdot \bigl(y_0^* I + \textstyle\sum_\lambda y_\lambda^* \pi_\lambda - T\bigr) \;=\; 0

is a matrix equation. Its rank counts the active dual support—the number of Wedderburn blocks simultaneously coupled at the optimum. When the rank exceeds one, the confined state is a sum of operators from distinct blocks.
sec:confinement-selection-confinement-sd: Comparing the semidefinite program against its linear-programming relaxation determines which multi-strand correlation constraints survive scalar projection. It establishes LP-dual stability across the active Wedderburn support. It then proves algebraic primality for irreducible magic closures (noting the vacuous base case n = 1) and derives the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta cosine resummation comparing the Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) against the spectral-bridge log-ratio.
rem:confinement-sdp-vs-lp:
Remark Relation of the confinement SDP to the scalar LP. The scalar confinement LP restricts \Phi in the confinement SDP to the diagonal span of the NF basis \{b_i\} and drops the 2\times2 pair blocks. Equivalently, the LP is the SDP with the rank-1 restriction \Phi = \mathrm{diag}(x) and the simplification \pi_\lambda \mapsto \mathbf{1}_\lambda.

The LP is exact when every Wedderburn block is one-dimensional. In general, the LP provides a lower bound on the SDP and misses the multi-operator binding structure. For most baryonic and light-nuclear configurations, the Wedderburn decomposition has 1-dimensional blocks and the LP suffices. Magic-number and shell-closure configurations require the SDP.

  \Phi \succeq 0
  \;\wedge\;
  \mathrm{rank}\text{-content}(\Phi) \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^{|\mathcal{S}|}.

Solve this Mixed-Integer Semidefinite Program (MISDP) via continuous SDP relaxation combined with branch-and-cut. This strictly matches the confinement framework at every level of the hierarchy.
prop:confinement-topological:
Proposition A matrix inequality in the standard representation of H_3(q) (confinement LP evidence). Let \rho be the standard two-dimensional representation of H_3(q) over the Laurent ring \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], with q = t^2,

  \rho(\sigma_0) = \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  \rho(\sigma_1) = \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix},

and put L_+ = \rho(\sigma_0\sigma_1), L_- = \rho(\sigma_1\sigma_0). Then

  L_+^2 + L_-^2 \;\neq\; 2\,L_+ L_- ,

since the (0,0) entries differ: -1 on the left and 2q^2 on the right.

This inequality is the only part proved. It is offered as evidence for the confinement linear program of prop:confinement-lp; the claims that the program over the Gram matrix of H_3(q) at q_0 has optimal value 0, that its optimum lies outside the image of B_3, and that \mathcal{B}_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 is the unique braid of length \le 6 hitting n_{\mathrm{target}} for both nucleons, are not part of this statement.
prf:confinement-topological:
Proof Proof of the standard-representation matrix inequality. Direct multiplication of the 2\times 2 generating matrices over \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}] (with q = t^2 and q^{-1} = t^{-2}) gives

  L_+
  = \rho(\sigma_0)\rho(\sigma_1)
  = \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix}
    \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix}
  = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & q \\ -q^{-1} & -1 \end{pmatrix}

and

  L_-
  = \rho(\sigma_1)\rho(\sigma_0)
  = \begin{pmatrix} -q^{-1} & 0 \\ 1 & q \end{pmatrix}
    \begin{pmatrix} q & 1 \\ 0 & -q^{-1} \end{pmatrix}
  = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -q^{-1} \\ q & 0 \end{pmatrix}.

Squaring L_+ and L_- and forming the mixed product L_+ L_- yields

  L_+^2 = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & -q \\ q^{-1} & 0 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  L_-^2 = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & q^{-1} \\ -q & -1 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  L_+ L_- = \begin{pmatrix} q^2 & 0 \\ q^{-1} - q & q^{-2} \end{pmatrix}.

Adding the squares and scaling the mixed product by 2,

  L_+^2 + L_-^2
  = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & q^{-1} - q \\ q^{-1} - q & -1 \end{pmatrix},
  \qquad
  2\,L_+ L_-
  = \begin{pmatrix} 2q^2 & 0 \\ 2(q^{-1} - q) & 2q^{-2} \end{pmatrix}.

At entry (0,0), the left-hand matrix has Laurent polynomial -1 = -t^0 \in \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], whose degree-4 coefficient is 0, whereas the right-hand matrix has 2q^2 = 2t^4 \in \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], whose degree-4 coefficient is 2 \neq 0. Hence -1 \neq 2q^2 in \mathbb{Z}[t^{\pm 1}], and therefore L_+^2 + L_-^2 \neq 2\,L_+ L_-.
rem:confinement-topological-interpretati:
Remark Confinement = topology + action minimization. The inequality L_+^2 + L_-^2 \neq 2\,L_+ L_- records noncommutativity of the length-two generators L_+ = \sigma_0\sigma_1 and L_- = \sigma_1\sigma_0 inside the two-dimensional standard module of H_3(q), where L_+ L_- \neq L_- L_+. Under the symmetric Markov-trace bilinear form G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i b_j) on the six-dimensional normal-form basis of H_3(q) at loop weight z = q^3/(q^2+1), the difference v_- = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(e_{L_+} - e_{L_-}) spans the unique negative-eigenvalue direction (\lambda_-(q) = -\lambda_+(q) < 0 for q > 1), while the three-row antisymmetric sector (1^3) spans the one-dimensional trace radical (\lambda_0(q) = 0).

This bilinear indefiniteness does not by itself force optimal value 0 or select a unique braid in the linear program of prop:confinement-lp. Because the basis begins with the unit element \mathbf{1}, the trace vector t_j = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_j) coincides with row 0 of G, so t \cdot x = (Gx)_0 \geq 0 holds throughout the cone Gx \geq 0; moreover t \cdot v_- = (Gv_-)_0 = 0 and Gv_- carries opposite-sign entries on L_+ and L_-. prop:shell-closure-stability:
Proposition Shell closure stability: categorical shell closures are local terminal objects. Fix a bare nuclear confined particle P_{\mathrm{bare}} at level \ell = 2 with atomic number Z_{\max}. Consider the dressing chain in the confinement category:

  P_{\mathrm{bare}}
  \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{S_1}}\;
  P^{(1)}
  \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{S_2}}\;
  \cdots
  \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dress}_{S_{Z_{\max}}}}\;
  P^{(Z_{\max})},

where P^{(Z)} is the dressed particle with Z attached electrons. Let \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) denote the Frobenius stability index, the optimal dual objective value of the confinement SDP at P^{(Z)}:

  \sigma_F(P, q)
  \;:=\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^*(P, q),

where u_0^*(P, q) is the optimal shadow price of the normalisation constraint. By strong duality, \sigma_F(P, q) coincides with the optimal primal objective \langle T, \Phi^*(P, q) \rangle and with the minimum-action Markov-trace weight of the confined operator. Then:

  1. Monotonic non-decrease. \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) is non-decreasing in Z along the dressing chain for every real q > 1 in the generic locus.
  2. Marginal gain maxima. The marginal stability gain \Delta\sigma_F(Z) := \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q) - \sigma_F(P^{(Z-1)}, q) attains a strict local maximum at each categorical shell closure, where the binding multiplicity satisfies \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2. While \sigma_F is monotone non-decreasing, its derivative \Delta\sigma_F peaks. The categorical closures occur precisely at the cumulative dimensions \{2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots\} of the representation sequence.
  3. Terminality. For every closure index Z \in \{2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots\}, P^{(Z)} is a local terminal object of the dressing sub-diagram. Any outgoing arrow \mathrm{dress}_{S'}: P^{(Z)} \to P' requires simultaneously breaking \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2 tight dual blocks of the confinement SDP.
prf:shell-closure-stability:
Proof Proof of shell closure stability. Scope of the dual-lift argument. Step 1 below contains an open gap: in the dual matrix inequality u_0 I + \sum_\lambda u_\lambda \pi_\lambda - T \preceq 0 with u_\lambda \ge 0, increasing a newly introduced multiplier u_\lambda adds a positive semidefinite term and tightens the inequality rather than relaxing it. The least restrictive choice on a new block is u_\lambda = 0, for which the dual lift is feasible only when u_0 I \preceq T_{\mathrm{new}} on that block—a domination bound not established here. Consequently, claim 1 of the proposition (and the monotonicity clause of claim 2 that rests on it) remains conditional on that block-domination bound, while step 3 compares the shell gap against the Archimedean quantity \alpha \cdot m_e \cdot c_q^2 across the evaluation wall.

One establishes three claims.

1. SDP-relaxation monotonicity. At each step Z - 1 \to Z, the dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_{S_Z} induces a cabling embedding \iota: H_{A + Z - 1}(q) \hookrightarrow H_{A + Z}(q). Three structural changes follow in the confinement SDP:

(a) Primal relaxation. The primal variable space extends from \mathrm{End}_R(H_{A+Z-1}(R, q)) to \mathrm{End}_R(H_{A+Z}(R, q)). The cabling-induced lift \Phi \mapsto \iota_* \Phi \oplus 0 embeds every primal-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_{Z-1} into the primal-feasible set of \mathrm{SDP}_Z, preserving the objective \langle T, \Phi \rangle.

(b) Dual relaxation. Dual variables extend by new shadow prices u_\lambda \ge 0 for every Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with k \in \{A+Z-1+1,\ldots, A+Z\} that first becomes available. Setting these new variables to zero recovers the old dual feasibility condition. Every dual-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_{Z-1} admits a lift to a dual-feasible point of \mathrm{SDP}_Z achieving the same objective n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0.

(c) Cost compatibility. The cost operator extends as a direct sum T^{(Z)} = \iota_* T^{(Z-1)} \oplus T_{\mathrm{new}}, where T_{\mathrm{new}} is the Markov-trace weight on the new block. Feasibility of the dual lift requires only that the additional u_\lambda^{(Z)} on the new blocks dominate T_{\mathrm{new}} in the matrix inequality u_0 I + \sum u_\lambda \pi_\lambda - T \preceq 0. Because T_{\mathrm{new}} is bounded and the new u_\lambda can take any non-negative value, a dominating choice always exists.

Because \mathrm{SDP}_Z maximises the dual objective over a superset of feasible points containing the lift of (u_0^{(Z-1)}, u_\lambda^{(Z-1)}), standard SDP-relaxation monotonicity gives

  \sigma_F(P^{(Z)}, q)
  \;=\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^{*(Z)}
  \;\ge\;
  n_{\mathrm{target}} \cdot u_0^{*(Z-1)}
  \;=\;
  \sigma_F(P^{(Z-1)}, q).

(Cost compatibility makes the lift feasible, ensuring the relaxation argument holds despite constraints added by dressing).

2. Local maxima. For Z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{noble}}, the orbital parametrisation of the electron shell fills all magnetic and spin labels of principal shell n. Multiple Wedderburn blocks of the multi-level SDP are simultaneously tight: \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2. Simultaneous tightness means the active-support Gram matrix has a rank-\mu dual kernel. By confinement-topological, the corresponding Frobenius form is non-degenerate on the complementary subspace (the complement is taken inside H_n/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, since the radical blocks are degenerate for the trace and would otherwise sit in every complement), and its minimum eigenvalue strictly exceeds the single-block value. This shell-boundary spectral-gap jump equals the strict local maximum of the marginal gain \Delta\sigma_F; \sigma_F itself stays monotone.

3. Terminality. An outgoing dressing \mathrm{dress}_{S'}: P^{(Z)} \to P' with Z \in \mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{noble}} extends the active support by opening a block of principal shell n + 1. Because the n-th shell is fully closed, no dual variable in shell n can slack. The extension is feasible only if every dual variable in shell n increases; every currently tight block must break to admit the new one. The energetic cost of breaking \mu(S_Z, q) \ge 2 tight blocks is at least \mu \cdot \Delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}(q). For q in the generic locus, \mu \cdot \Delta E_{\mathrm{shell}}(q) > \alpha \cdot m_e \cdot c_q^2. No electromagnetic-mediated dressing clears the barrier, making P^{(Z)} terminal within the \mathrm{dress} sub-diagram. \square

Its marginal increment \Delta\sigma_F(Z) = I_1(Z) has local maxima at the categorical shell closures [2, 10, 28, 60, \ldots].

prop:level-sufficiency:
Proposition Level sufficiency: Markov trace computable in the coarsest confinement algebra. Let P = (\mathrm{name}, \ell, [K]_M, n_0) be a confined particle and let

  \uparrow_\ell \colon P \longrightarrow P^{\uparrow}
  \quad\text{with}\quad
  P^{\uparrow} = (\mathrm{name}, \ell - 1, [\iota(K)]_M, n_1)

be an unfolding morphism in the confinement category, where \iota: H_{n_0}(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_1}(R, q) is the Hecke inclusion and n_1 \ge n_0. If the coarse witnessed partition truncation satisfies

  k_{\max}(P, q) \le n_0

then the Markov trace is preserved along the unfolding:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(T_w^{\downarrow}\right)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\left(T_w^{\uparrow}\right)
  \quad\text{in }\mathbb{C}(q),

where T_w^{\downarrow} \in H_{n_0}(q) and T_w^{\uparrow} \in H_{n_1}(q) are the Gröbner–Shirshov normal forms of K at coarse and fine levels respectively. Consequently, every trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} of P takes the same value on P and P^{\uparrow}:

  \mathcal{F}(P) \;=\; \mathcal{F}(P^{\uparrow}).

The coarsest level at which k_{\max}(P, q, n) \le n is computationally sufficient. Unfolding to any deeper level is superfluous for trace-class invariants.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
prf:level-sufficiency:
Proof Proof of level sufficiency. The Ocneanu–Jones Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M: H_\bullet(q) \to \mathbb{C}(q) is a compatible family along the Hecke tower H_n(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n+1}(R, q). It satisfies the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M \circ \iota = \mathrm{tr}_M (Jones 1987). Hypothesis k_{\max}(P, q) \le n_0 asserts that every Wedderburn block \lambda \vdash k with k > n_0 has zero projection in T_w^{\downarrow}. Under the inclusion \iota: H_{n_0}(R, q) \hookrightarrow H_{n_1}(R, q) this vanishing is preserved. The additional blocks \lambda \vdash k with n_0 < k \le n_1 accessible at the fine level contribute zero to T_w^{\uparrow} = \iota\,T_w^{\downarrow}. Thus \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\uparrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\iota\,T_w^{\downarrow}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\downarrow}) by the Markov property. Functoriality of \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q) (confinement category) extends this equality to every composite of unfoldings, establishing preservation along the full confinement chain.

For a general trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} that factors through \mathrm{tr}_M, equality of traces implies equality of values: \mathcal{F}(P^{\uparrow}) = \mathcal{F}(P). \square

Converse (unfolding necessity). If k_{\max}(P, q) > n_0 — the witnessed partition content of P exceeds the coarse strand count — then no representation of T_w^{\downarrow} as an element of H_{n_0}(q) captures all tight dual blocks of the confinement SDP. Unfolding to the smallest level n_1 with k_{\max}(P, q, n_1) \le n_1 is strictly required. The unfolded trace \mathrm{tr}_M(T_w^{\uparrow}) differs from any coarse surrogate by contributions from the additional blocks. Magic shell closure and multi-operator binding configurations (\mu(S, q) \ge 2) are the principal triggers.

Corollary (default-coarse computability). Every trace-class invariant \mathcal{F} computed at the coarsest level satisfying k_{\max} \le n is exact. Default-coarse computation is not a performance heuristic. It is the content of this proposition.
rem:level-sufficiency-interprets:
Remark Physical interpretation of level sufficiency: default coarse, unfold on witness. This proposition is the formal justification for a default-coarse computational strategy across the full confinement category. The hierarchy has at least four relevant levels:

At each level, any trace-class invariant is exact at the coarsest representation satisfying k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) \le n_0.

Default-coarse rule. Every computational pipeline executes the following steps:

  1. Identify the confined particle P at its natural level \ell.
  2. Read k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) from the witness data.
  3. If k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) \le n_0, compute \mathrm{tr}_M at the coarse level and halt.
  4. If k_{\max}(P, q, n_0) > n_0, apply the unfolding morphism \uparrow_\ell and repeat at \ell - 1.

  • Magic shell closure. Atoms at A \in \{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\} and noble-gas electron counts Z \in \{2, 10, 18, 36, 54, 86\} exhibit binding multiplicity \mu(S, q) \ge 2. This forces k_{\max} above the coarse count. Atoms in these rows evaluate one level deeper.
  • SDP cross-channel demand. The active dual support \mathcal{S}^* of the confinement SDP spans blocks \lambda_1, \lambda_2. When \max(|\lambda_1|, |\lambda_2|) > n_0, the coarse representation cannot express the coupling. Unfolding is required.

Non-magic atoms and molecules without SDP cross-channel demand evaluate at their natural coarse level. This is the minimal exact representation.

Dressing preserves computational minimality. Under the dressing morphism \mathrm{dress}_S: P_{\mathrm{bare}} \to P_{\mathrm{dressed}}, the witnessed truncation updates to

  k_{\max}(P_{\mathrm{dressed}}, q)
  \;=\;
  \max\bigl(k_{\max}(P_{\mathrm{bare}}, q),\;
            k_{\max}^{\mathrm{bind}}(S, q)\bigr),

where k_{\max}^{\mathrm{bind}} is the partition reach of the binding subword W_{\mathrm{bind}}. The dressed particle's computational level follows from the updated k_{\max}. Adding a single electron to a non-magic atom typically leaves the computational level unchanged. Closing to a noble gas triggers \mu \ge 2 and raises the required level.

Default-coarse computation is the computational content of this proposition applied via the confinement category.
prop:confinement-phase-stratification:
Proposition The confinement locus is open, and the active support is constant on a strictly complementary phase. Let P be a confined particle, and let the aether parameter q range over \mathbb{R}_{>1}. Write strict feasibility of the confinement SDP as a finite system of strict inequalities 0 < g_i(q, X), i \in I, in q and the decision variable X, with each g_i continuous. (Positive definiteness of a Gram matrix is such a system, by Sylvester's criterion on its leading principal minors.) The confinement locus of P is

  \Omega(P) \;:=\; \{\, q : \exists X,\ \forall i \in I,\ 0 < g_i(q, X) \,\}.

Let u^*_\lambda(q) be the dual variables of the SDP and s_\lambda(q) the matching primal slacks. The active support is \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) := \{\lambda : u^*_\lambda(q) > 0\} and the binding multiplicity is \mu(P, q) := |\mathcal{S}^*(P, q)|. Then:

  1. Openness. \Omega(P) is open.
  2. Constancy on a phase. Let C \subseteq \Omega(P) be connected. Suppose u^*_\lambda and s_\lambda are continuous in q, complementary (u^*_\lambda s_\lambda = 0) and strictly complementary (u^*_\lambda > 0 or s_\lambda > 0) at every q \in C. Then \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) and \mu(P, q) are constant on C.

The remaining structure of the phases (the boundary stratification, analyticity of the Frobenius stability index, scope and phase transitions) is stated separately in the phase-boundary conjecture below.

Archimedean specialisation. Both parts sit on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall: the locus is a subset of \mathbb{R}, and openness and connectedness are statements about the real topology.
prf:confinement-phase-stratification:
Proof Proof of confinement phase stratification. Claim (1)—Openness. Let S := \{(q, X) : \forall i,\ 0 < g_i(q, X)\}. Each set \{0 < g_i\} is open because g_i is continuous, and I is finite, so S is open. \Omega(P) is the image of S under the projection (q, X) \mapsto q, which is an open map. Hence \Omega(P) is open.

Claim (2)—Constancy on a phase. Fix \lambda. Let U := \{q : u^*_\lambda(q) > 0\} and V := \{q : s_\lambda(q) > 0\}; both are open by continuity. Strict complementarity gives C \subseteq U \cup V. If C met both U and V, then, C being connected, it would meet U \cap V at some q; there u^*_\lambda(q)\, s_\lambda(q) > 0, contradicting complementarity. So either u^*_\lambda > 0 on all of C, or u^*_\lambda > 0 nowhere on C. This holds for every \lambda, so \mathcal{S}^*(P, q) is the same set for every q \in C, and so is its size \mu(P, q). \square
rem:confinement-phase-stratification-int: Remark Topology of the confinement locus \Omega(P). For simple particles, \Omega(P) is expected to be a single connected interval of \mathbb{R}_{>1} containing q_0; neither connectedness nor q_0 \in \Omega(P) is proved. For composite particles with multi-block binding, \Omega(P) can be disconnected. Each component corresponds to a distinct configuration of the active support. One physically realises transitions between components as chemical or nuclear rearrangements. Computationally, they appear as regime switches in the witness files.
conj:confinement-phase-boundaries:
Conjecture Phase boundaries of the confinement locus. Let P be a confined particle, with confinement locus \Omega(P), active support \mathcal{S}^*(P, q), binding multiplicity \mu(P, q) and Frobenius stability index \sigma_F(P, q) as in prop:confinement-phase-stratification. Let \mathcal{G} \subset \mathbb{R}_{>1} be the generic locus of q, and call a connected component \Omega_\alpha of \Omega(P) a confinement phase. Then:

  1. Stratification. The complement \mathcal{G} \setminus \Omega(P) is a real-algebraic stratification with strata of codimension \ge 1, the phase boundaries of P. Each stratum is the zero locus of a principal minor of the SDP Gram matrix.
  2. Strict complementarity on phases. On each phase \Omega_\alpha the SDP dual pair is continuous and strictly complementary, so the active support and \mu are constant on \Omega_\alpha by prop:confinement-phase-stratification.
  3. Analyticity. \sigma_F(P, q) is real-analytic on each \Omega_\alpha.
  4. Scope. Level sufficiency, shell-closure stability and the Markov-trace preservation of the confinement category functor hold pointwise in each \Omega_\alpha and fail on \partial\Omega(P).
  5. Phase transitions. If a continuous path q: [0, 1] \to \mathcal{G} crosses a phase boundary at q_0 \in \partial\Omega(P), then at q_0 either P is not realisable as a closed-braid bound state (deconfinement), or \mu jumps, the active support gains or loses a Wedderburn block, and \sigma_F has a non-smooth point (regime switch), or both.

Supporting argument (not a proof). For (1): the entries of the Gram matrix are Laurent polynomials in q, so each principal minor that is not identically zero has finitely many real zeros in \mathcal{G}; what is not shown is that loss of strict feasibility happens exactly on these zero sets. For (2): strict complementarity holds for generic SDP data (Alizadeh–Haeberly–Overton), but genericity at the aether parameters is not established. For (4): the proofs of prop:level-sufficiency and prop:shell-closure-stability use a well-defined, locally constant active support. For (5): a boundary crossing is either a loss of strict primal feasibility or a dual variable u^*_\lambda passing through zero.
rem:phase-scoped-applicability:
Remark Phase-scoped applicability: confinement theorems hold on open strata only. The phase-boundary conjecture (conj:confinement-phase-boundaries) proposes the scope caveat attached to every statement in the confinement framework. Any formal statement about a confined particle P, its electron shell, a dressing morphism, or a trace-class invariant \mathcal{F}(P) includes the implicit quantifier:

  \forall\, q \in \Omega_\alpha(P),

where \Omega_\alpha(P) is a fixed connected component of the confinement locus \Omega(P), a single confinement phase.

Conjecturally phase-scoped results (conjectured to hold only within a single \Omega_\alpha):

  • Level sufficiency: preservation of Markov trace under unfolding.
  • Shell-closure stability: monotonicity of \sigma_F along the dressing chain and local maxima at noble-gas Z.
  • Functoriality of \mathrm{tr}_M: \mathbf{Conf} \to \mathbb{C}(q).
  • Multi-operator binding structure: constancy of the active support.

Boundary phenomena (not covered by the phase-scoped results):

  • Deconfinement events. At q \in \partial\Omega(P) with Slater-strict feasibility lost, P ceases to be realisable as a closed-braid bound state.
  • Regime switches. At q \in \partial\Omega(P) with a \mu-jump but preserved feasibility, the active support gains or loses a Wedderburn block.
  • Critical scaling. Near a phase boundary, \sigma_F typically has a non-analytic limit.
  • Chemical and nuclear rearrangements. Transitions between disconnected components of \Omega(P) for a composite P are realised physically as structural rearrangements. These transitions require an explicit cross-component analysis using the stratification of \Omega(P).

Practical reading. When encountering a confinement-framework statement, treat q as ranging over a fixed open phase unless the text addresses boundary behaviour. Numerical witnesses evaluate at a single q = q_0 \approx 1.110. As long as that point lies in \Omega_\alpha(P), the phase-scoped results apply wherever they hold. Auditing behaviour across q ranges requires explicit stratification analysis.

prop:lp-dual-stability:
Proposition LP dual stability: the confined optimum is LP-stable and strongly dual. Let x^* \in \mathbb{R}^6 be an optimum of the operator-selection linear program

  \min_x \; t^\top x
  \quad\text{subject to}\quad
  \sum_i x_i = n_{\mathrm{target}}, \qquad G x \geq 0, \qquad x \geq 0,

where G is the Frobenius Gram matrix and t is the mass-coefficient vector, so that t^\top x^* = \mathrm{tr}_M(x^*). Then:

  1. x^* is LP-stable: Gx^* \geq 0 in all six channels.
  2. Strong duality holds: there is a dual optimum whose net-constraint shadow price y_0^* satisfies \mathrm{tr}_M(x^*) = y_0^* \cdot n_{\mathrm{target}}.

Both parts hold for every Gram matrix G and cost vector t. Part 1 is the feasibility of x^*, and part 2 is finite-dimensional linear-programming strong duality. The confinement-specific properties of the six-channel matrix at the aether are recorded in the confinement reading.
rem:lp-dual-stability-confinement-readin:
Remark Confinement reading of the LP-dual stability criterion. Two further properties are claimed for the specific six-channel Gram matrix at the aether. They are not derived from linear-programming duality, and they are not currently established numerically: the Gram matrix built by the confinement operator-selection computation is singular, so it has no finite condition number, and that computation does not produce shadow prices. They are recorded here rather than in the proposition:

  • The dual shadow prices are bounded by |y_i^*| \leq \kappa(G) \cdot \|t\|, where \kappa(G) is the condition number of G (a value \approx 7.0 was recorded earlier, but the Gram matrix the computation now builds is singular, so this figure is not reproduced). Linear-programming duality alone does not bound shadow prices by the condition number, so the bound would have to come from the matrix itself; for a singular G (\kappa(G) = \infty) it says nothing.
  • The B_3 sub-braid \sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1} is LP-unstable: G\vec{x} has a negative \sigma_0 component. Partial confinement is therefore not sufficient, and all three units are required.

Individual quarks are LP-stable and the B_3 sub-unit is LP-unstable. In this reading, that is what confinement means algebraically: the gluon field contains an LP-unstable intermediate, and stability returns only for the full 3-fold Borromean product. Stability of the binding operator therefore requires the topologically complete structure; the B_3 sub-unit alone is not enough.

The negative eigenvalue \lambda_{\min} \approx -0.956 (a historical figure; the canonical-weight value is \approx -0.7527, see the Frobenius Gram matrix) gives the LP, without the braid constraint, a global minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. def:algebraic-primality:
Definition Algebraic primality of a strand count. Fix an aether parameter q > 1. For each strand count n \geq 1, the confinement SDP selects a canonical state \psi_n(q). Say that n is algebraically prime at q if \psi_n(q) is not contained in the closed span of any non-trivial tensor product

  \overline{\mathrm{span}}\bigl\{\,
    \psi_{n_1}(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes \psi_{n_k}(q)
  \,\bigr\}.

This product is indexed by a decomposition n = n_1 + \cdots + n_k with k \geq 2 and every n_i \geq 1.
rem:algebraic-primality-remark:
Remark Algebraic primality as a magic-number surrogate. By convention, n = 0 is not prime. This predicate serves as a purely algebraic surrogate for a magic strand count. An algebraically prime configuration does not factor into a product of smaller closed configurations.

The definition relies on a recursive decomposition argument. Testing primality at n checks all decompositions into smaller parts. The recursion bottoms out at n = 1. The n=1 state is algebraically prime vacuously, because no decomposition into k \geq 2 positive parts sums to 1.
prop:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic:
Proposition Vacuous primality at n = 1. For every aether q > 1, the integer n = 1 is algebraically prime. Equivalently, the canonical state \psi_1(q) is not in the closed span of any non-trivial tensor product of canonical states indexed by a decomposition 1 = n_1 + \cdots + n_k with k \geq 2 and n_i \geq 1. No such decomposition exists.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall.
rem:n-equals-1-vacuous-magic-context:
Remark Base case, empirical magic numbers, and archimedean scope of vacuous primality. The proof uses only elementary arithmetic. It uses no SDP analysis, Hecke-algebra machinery, or tensor-product manipulation. This is the base case of the recursion. Every primality check at n \geq 2 ultimately bottoms out at n = 1 through repeated decomposition.

Empirical nuclear magic numbers start at 2. The framework's n = 1 primality is sometimes glossed as below the lowest shell closure. Within the algebraic-primality framework, n = 1 is strictly magic, just for a vacuous reason.

The archimedean specialisation invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs. Any generic categorical identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
